subject: ACME inference playbook: dedicated sizing, burst fallback & next tests
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: ACME discovery — capacity & hyperscaler comparison

Hi team,

Quick recap from the call with Jordan / Priya at ACME earlier today. High-level: they are evaluating Redwood Dedicated against their current hyperscaler reservations (GCP/Azure) and want clarity on the following before procurement:

- Capacity guarantees (reserved pools vs reserved instances) and how we handle burst beyond committed capacity
- Predictable unit costs for their high-throughput embedding workload (monthly cost modeling)
- Fall back behavior when Dedicated pool is saturated (routing, model variants, hosted API fallback)
- Security/compliance evidence (SOC2 and private VPC option) — they flagged procurement will ask for this

They asked for a short, actionable playbook and a set of tests we can run in the next 2 weeks to compare:
1) Latency-sensitive chat (p95 target) across typical session lengths (64/256 tokens)
2) Bulk embedding throughput (tokens/sec and cost per 1M tokens)
3) Failure/fallback scenario (simulate pool exhaustion and measure failover time and quality)

As next steps I promised:
- A one-page POC scope + test plan (attached)
- A cost-comparison matrix vs their reserved instance pricing (attached)
- Suggested Dedicated sizing and minimal commit recommendations

Questions for you both: can you review the attached scope and sizing recommendation and confirm what minimal commit (GPUs / vram) we can offer for a 4-week trial? Also, what burst policy options can we present (hard cap vs. graceful degrade + hosted fallback)?

I'll log this as DEAL-ACME-9831 in HubSpot and coordinate procurement artifacts once we have the numbers.

Thanks,
Rafael
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: ACME discovery — capacity & hyperscaler comparison

Thanks for the summary, Rafael — good call. A few tactical notes on the test plan and fallback behavior:

- Test design: please include a warmup window (30–60 min) to populate KV caches and measure steady-state throughput. For embeddings, run at least 100k requests per workload to get stable cost numbers.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/s, GPU occupancy, KV cache hit rate, and end-to-end error rate per minute.
- Dedicated sizing: for the embedding workload shown in the matrix, my recommendation is 4 x A10G-equivalent slots (quantized/8-bit) for the trial. That maps to ~160k embeddings/day at target latency and gives room for modest burst.
- Burst/fallback: offer two options to ACME: 1) Reserved + burst credits (best for predictable workloads) or 2) Reserved with graceful degradation: automatic routing to a compatible, slightly lower-capacity model variant + short-lived hosted fallback when the pool is saturated (we can limit to safety and rate-limited fallback).
- Failover test: we should include a scenario where we intentionally cap the pool (simulate 0 available slots) and measure time to reroute to the hosted API and p95 jump. Expectation: reroute under our routing policy should take < 2s for request requeue + model spin-up if needed; document the exact steps and fallback rate limits.

I attached a short markdown with sizing rationale and the quantization profile I'm proposing. I also think we should offer ACME a short SLA note: committed throughput target for the trial, and an explicit escalation path if we miss those numbers.

I'll coordinate with infra to confirm actual slot availability next week.

- Monica
Head of Dedicated Solutions
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: ACME discovery — capacity & hyperscaler comparison

Quick update on capacity availability and lead times:

- We can provision a 4-slot Dedicated pool (A10G-equivalent) for a 4-week trial starting as early as 2026-06-22. If ACME wants stronger headroom, a 6-slot pool is feasible but needs a 7–10 day lead time for reserved capacity scheduling.
- Burst model: we can support a burst buffer backed by our hosted capacity with per-customer burst credits. For procurement language, call it "overflow burst credits" limited to X tokens/day (we'll fill exact X after Rafael confirms target volume).
- SLA: For a trial we can commit to an internal SLO of 99% request success for provisioned capacity. For formal SLA language (enterprise contract) we need legal to review — that will take longer.
- Procurement note: for Reserved pools we typically ask for monthly commitment in GPU-hours. For short trials we can do a prepaid 4-week invoice and convert to committed monthly billing later if they opt-in.

I'll tentatively reserve the earlier start date (22 Jun) for ACME, subject to Rafael confirming the commit. Also: we should include SOC2 and network diagrams in the procurement package — Rafael, add that request to the HubSpot ticket and I'll attach from Security.

- Logan
Director, Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Rafael / team — thanks for the clear plan and apologies for the slower reply.

We're aligned on running a short POC. A couple of constraints from procurement and engineering:
- Procurement needs SOC2 report and our standard vendor questionnaire returned before payment terms can be agreed. Can you send the SOC2 evidence and a contact for Redwood procurement?
- Engineering would like the 4-slot trial start (22 Jun) if we can lock it. We will run both chat and embedding workloads as discussed. Please include the failover test and the hosted fallback routing in the scope.
- Budget: we can do a one-time prepaid 4-week trial under our Q3 evaluation budget, but will need committed monthly costs and minimal term details on the follow-up contract before end of Q3.

If you can send the procurement artifacts and a short one-page test acceptance criteria doc by EOD Wed (17 Jun), we can turn this around quickly and get finance to release the trial payment.

Cheers,
Jordan Ellis
Head of AI Platforms
ACME Corp.
